newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: FORECAST-Slump seen for CHH first half.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Slump seen for CHH first half.

text.p: New Zealand forestry group Carter Holt Harvey Ltd's earnings are expected to slump to around NZ$115-125 million in the first half to September from NZ$271.0 million for the same period a year ago, analysts said on Monday.
Depressed log, pulp and paper prices are expected to be the main drivers, although flatness in the Australasian building cycle may also come into play.
Frances Loo at SBC Warburg expected second quarter earnings to come in at around NZ$68 million from $56 million in the first quarter.

Forestry and oil conglomerate Compania de Petroleos de Chile (Copec), whose own profit in the first nine months of 1996 slumped to 77.46 billion pesos from 152.95 billion, was expected to further dampen CHH's earnings.
"Commodity markets will obviously have an impact," Loo said, adding there was anecdotal evidence of a slowing in the New Zealand domestic economy in the run up to the October 12 election.

"It's fair to say that although the industry globally has pretty much bottomed, there's been no quick turnaround," Loo said. "Clearly the company will not be delivering its full profit potential, given the state of those key markets."
John Cairns, head of research at Cavill White Securities, said pulp, and more importantly, log prices would play a big part. He expects a first half net profit of around NZ$115-120 million.
"Hopefully, the bottom of the cycle should not be too far away. Pulp and paper is at an interesting time," said one Wellington analyst.

Other issues facing CHH are its dispute with the Angelini group in Chile, through which CHH holds a 30 percent stake in Copec. CHH is seeking board representation at Copec but has so far been thwarted by litigation.
There was also ongoing speculation that CHH's majority shareholder, International Paper, may soon take advantage of CHH's low share price and buy the remaining stock it does not already own.
IP is known to favour full control of its units, not the 50.1 percent stake it has at present. IP's last foray into CHH was at NZ$3.80 a share against today's price of $3.23.
